StatementExtracted: Check that the router and connected equipment are switched on and powered.
InterpretationForSystem: A missing-power indication is only used after the external power supply has been checked.

StatementExtracted: TP-Link says an Internet LED that is off or a WAN-port-unplugged message can indicate a WAN/hardware-connection issue; it advises checking the WAN cable and testing the modem directly.
InterpretationForSystem: R09 uses the TP-Link Internet-light-off state only. A normal broadband indicator and secure incoming cable are additional rule conditions that narrow its use, not claims attributed to TP-Link. The result is a possible WAN connection issue, not a confirmed router fault; a direct-modem test is recommended to distinguish router, modem and provider problems.

StatementExtracted: Check that the cable between the incoming socket or fibre equipment and router is firmly connected.
InterpretationForSystem: A loose cable is checked before diagnosing router or access-equipment problems; equipment restart evidence is interpreted according to access type.

StatementExtracted: Restarting router or modem equipment may restore a temporary connection problem.
InterpretationForSystem: The system records a restart of the separate DSL modem or fibre ONT separately from a router restart. Applying general equipment-restart guidance to a separate DSL modem is a project-designed check, not a source-specific instruction for every standalone modem.

StatementExtracted: Use device scope and an Ethernet comparison to help separate a shared access failure from a Wi-Fi-only problem.
InterpretationForSystem: All-device impact plus failed wired access derives a shared-connection fact.

StatementExtracted: Ofcom and BT advise checking broadband equipment indicators and the phone line when broadband service stops.
InterpretationForSystem: R06 requires repeated DSL synchronisation loss and either a poor phone line or (when the whole household also fails on a wired connection) a model-specific broadband indicator identified as abnormal using the equipment's own guidance. This combined corroboration condition is designed by the project and is not a diagnostic relationship explicitly established by S01 or S02.

StatementExtracted: Openreach guidance says solid-green PON with LOS off is normal and identifies specified PON-off/flashing or red-LOS patterns as warnings. BT distinguishes PON flashing with LOS off as verification, gives model-specific indicator layouts, and says all Ethernet Port lights off may indicate a missing or broken cable to the Hub.
InterpretationForSystem: The system treats PON flashing with LOS off as verification, following BT's more specific combined-light guidance. R10 fires only when PON is off, LOS is red, or PON and LOS are both flashing. PON red and other combinations remain unclassified. For a Nokia observation with the Port indicator off, the system gives a separate Ethernet-cable check; this observation does not activate R10 or establish a fibre-link fault. ECI Optical states and other indicator layouts not represented by the questionnaire remain unknown rather than being mapped to PON/LOS conditions.

StatementExtracted: A noisy or absent landline tone can indicate a phone-line problem.
InterpretationForSystem: Poor dial tone is used only with repeated DSL synchronisation loss; a phone-only symptom is not treated as a broadband line fault.

StatementExtracted: A microfilter is required on some single-socket copper installations and omission can cause broadband or telephone problems.
InterpretationForSystem: This is a local setup check, not a diagnostic rule. If the socket requires a filter and it is missing, the explanation recommends fitting the correct filter; omission alone does not establish a provider-side line fault.

StatementExtracted: Persistent line symptoms after basic router restart checks should be reported to the provider.
InterpretationForSystem: Repeated DSL synchronisation loss plus unsuccessful router restart supports line investigation.

StatementExtracted: Check the provider service-status page or app for a known outage.
InterpretationForSystem: A provider-confirmed outage is retained as a direct status-based rule.

StatementExtracted: Outage-checking services may show reports from other customers, but these are user reports rather than network measurements.
InterpretationForSystem: Require both a shared household access failure and local reports; label the result possible rather than confirmed.

StatementExtracted: A provider may restrict or suspend a service and display an explicit restriction message.
InterpretationForSystem: Only an explicit provider account status is used; an overdue bill by itself is insufficient.

StatementExtracted: Ofcom advises comparing a device that is slower than others with the other devices and checking the affected device itself.
InterpretationForSystem: R15 adds a project-designed cross-network check: if the same device also fails on another Wi-Fi network, a device-side problem becomes more plausible. Ofcom supports device comparison but does not prescribe this specific cross-network test.

StatementExtracted: Apple explains how its devices prioritise known wireless networks and use Auto-Join settings.
InterpretationForSystem: The general rule checks whether one device reconnects to a saved network. Apple's Auto-Join instructions apply to Apple devices; equivalent settings and names on other devices vary and are not established by S07.

StatementExtracted: Ofcom advises comparing an affected device with other devices. The BT Community thread reports authentication failures on some devices and successful connections on others, but does not establish that these occurred simultaneously.
InterpretationForSystem: R16 adds project-designed checks: re-enter the current password and compare whether another device can join. These checks distinguish persistent rejection from a typing error; the sources provide general device-comparison guidance and reported symptoms, not this complete test sequence.

StatementExtracted: Distance and physical obstacles can reduce Wi-Fi performance.
InterpretationForSystem: Use this only after a wired-working/Wi-Fi-failing comparison establishes a wireless-path problem.

StatementExtracted: Nearby electronics and radio sources can interfere with wireless performance.
InterpretationForSystem: Treat nearby interference as a possible contributor only when wired access works and Wi-Fi fails.

StatementExtracted: A working Ethernet connection alongside failed Wi-Fi points towards the wireless part of the home connection.
InterpretationForSystem: Derive a wireless-path fact; later rules distinguish coverage, interference and whole-house Wi-Fi symptoms.

StatementExtracted: Data-heavy downloads, updates and streaming can use household bandwidth.
InterpretationForSystem: A reported slowdown plus concurrent heavy use supports a possible household-congestion explanation.

StatementExtracted: Broadband speed can vary at different times; repeated tests are needed to identify a pattern.
InterpretationForSystem: A reported slowdown plus a recurring busy-period pattern supports possible peak-time congestion, without locating the bottleneck.

StatementExtracted: The provider remains responsible for handling a reported broadband service fault.
InterpretationForSystem: Used for escalation advice; it does not create a diagnostic condition.

StatementExtracted: A clear provider status page does not prove that no fault exists; a fault may not yet be logged.
InterpretationForSystem: Retained as a limitation in the explanation and report.

StatementExtracted: Restart advice is a troubleshooting action and does not by itself establish a defective router.
InterpretationForSystem: Recovery after restarting an access unit is recorded against the specific unit and does not establish that a router is defective.

StatementExtracted: A recent noisy or absent landline can leave an ADSL connection at a reduced rate after the noise clears; the provider can investigate and reset the line profile.
InterpretationForSystem: Only a copper/ADSL connection with reported recent line noise and an explicit slowdown activates R25; a current clear dial tone does not erase the recent event and slowdown alone is insufficient.
